sentences.text: The application for bail of the appellant has been rejected by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge -cum- Special Judge, Jharsuguda as per order dated 16.08.2024.

entities.text: Addl. Sessions Judge -cum- Special Judge, Jharsuguda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was taken into judicial custody on 16.05.2021 and when he approached this Court for bail in CRLA No.376 of 2023, while not inclining to release the appellant on bail but taking into account the period of detention of the appellant in judicial custody, the learned trial Court was directed to expedite the trial and to conclude the same within a period of six months and the appellant was given liberty to renew the prayer for bail if the Chandrabhanu Prusty @ vs State Of Odisha on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23344030/
1 trial is not concluded within the said period.
Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that as on date, out of twenty four charge sheeted witnesses, five witnesses have been examined, but the informant-victim could not been examined as her whereabouts is not known.
As per the order dated 07.12.2024, this Court directed the I.I.C., Jharsuguda G.R.P.S. to appear before the learned trial Court on or before 20.12.2024 to receive summons in respect of the victim and to ensure her attendance on the date fixed.
Learned counsel for the appellant produced the order sheet of the learned trial Court dated 20.01.2025, wherein it is mentioned that the I.I.C., Jharsuguda G.R.P.S. submitted a report that the whereabouts of the victim is not known as stated by her family members.

entities.text: Chandrabhanu Prusty @ vs State Of Odisha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the prosecution was directed by the learned trial Court to furnish the whereabouts of the victim.
The certified copy of the order is taken on record.

Learned counsel for the State has also produced the report from the concerned police station before this Court, which indicates that the family members are not aware about the whereabouts of the victim.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, the period of detention of the appellant in judicial custody and since the order dated 16.10.2023 passed in CRLA No.376 of 2023 has not been complied with, while not inclining to release the appellant on bail on merit, but taking into account the period of detention in judicial custody and the inability of the prosecution to produce the victim before the trial Court to give her evidence, I am inclined to release the appellant on interim bail for a period of three months from the date of release.
The appellant shall immediately surrender before the learned trial Court on expiry of the said three months period.

For the above period, let the appellant be released on interim bail to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court in connection with the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount including the condition that he shall not indulge in any criminal activities while on interim bail.
Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of interim bail.
Accordingly, the CRLA is disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of this order as per Rules.
